section_1.title: Introduction: The 'Slow-Motion' Illusion
section_1.content: Hook the audience by illustrating light entering a medium. Briefly recall the definition: n = c/v. Establish that n > 1 implies light 'slows down' in materials. Prerequisite: Recall that light is an electromagnetic wave interacting with charged particles.
section_1.example: A straw appears broken in a glass of water; we explain this as light 'bending' due to the medium's density.

section_2.title: The Microscopic Origin: Induced Dipoles
section_2.content: Explain that light's oscillating electric field drives electrons in atoms to oscillate. These oscillating electrons re-radiate waves that interfere with the incident wave, resulting in a phase-shifted (slowed) superposition. Use an animation showing an incident wave hitting an electron cloud.
section_2.example: Think of a crowd of people (electrons) trying to pass a message; the 'dragging' effect caused by their interaction is what we perceive as a slower wave velocity.

section_3.title: The Dependence on Color: Dispersion
section_3.content: Introduce the concept of natural frequency (resonance) of atoms. Higher frequencies (blue light) interact more strongly than lower frequencies (red light). Display a graph showing the refractive index n(λ) vs. wavelength λ. Use a color-coded wave animation to show blue light oscillating 'tighter' against atomic structures.
section_3.example: A chameleon's specialized skin cells; they change color by manipulating the refractive index and structural interference of light.

section_4.title: Visualizing the Mathematics: The Sellmeier Equation
section_4.content: Introduce the Sellmeier equation conceptually. Emphasize how n depends on λ based on material constants. Provide a graphical representation: a plot showing curves where n peaks near absorption bands. Connect this to the physical reality that near resonance, refractive index changes rapidly.
section_4.example: Using a prism to split white light into a rainbow; the 'spread' of the colors is the direct physical manifestation of n varying by wavelength.

section_5.title: Conclusion and Real-World Application
section_5.content: Synthesize the two main points: 1. Refraction is a collective response of electrons. 2. Chromatic dependence is due to varying resonance strengths. Summarize how this determines the design of optical instruments.
section_5.example: Camera lenses: Designers must use 'Achromatic doublets' (two different glass types) to correct for the fact that blue and red light focus at different points due to dispersion.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
